title: What is Fantasy Fiction?
use_cases: Use when defining the core characteristics and boundaries of the fantasy genre
Implement when developing a secondary world with unique history, maps, and rules
Configure when integrating magic as a central plot device or supernatural force
Use when applying standard genre tropes like the chosen one or mentor archetypes
Configure when populating a narrative with non-human races such as elves or dwarves
content:
Let’s start with the one most people know. What is fantasy fiction? At its heart, fantasy is a genre that uses magic and other supernatural elements. These elements are a main part of the plot, the world, or the theme.

Think about the books you loved as a kid. Many are probably fantasy. The key characteristics of fantasy fiction are easy to spot. First, fantasy stories often happen in a “secondary world.” This is a world that is not Earth. It is a place the author made up from scratch. It has its own history. It has its own maps. It has its own rules. This is a huge part of the genre. Authors spend years on this. This is often called Tolkien-style world creation. J.R.R. Tolkien, who wrote The Lord of the Rings, is famous for this. He created languages, histories, and geographies for his world, Middle-earth.

In this separate world, magic is real. But it is also seen as supernatural. It is not part of everyday life for most people. It is special. It is powerful. It is often a skill that people must learn, like a wizard going to school. Or it is a power that certain beings have, like elves or dragons. When magic happens, characters in the story react. They might be scared. They might be in awe. They know it is not normal.

Fantasy stories often have fantasy genre tropes. These are common ideas or themes. You might see a “chosen one.” This is a hero who is destined to save the world. You might see a wise old mentor. You will almost always see a big fight between good and evil. There are often non-human races. Think of dwarves, elves, orcs, and hobbits. These are all signs you are reading fantasy. This kind of fantasy storytelling techniques creates big, epic stories. They are often about saving the world.
